task_family: before-after update version check / historical path retirement

recurrent_mechanisms.mechanism: Historical compatibility review remains explicitly authorized by the cleanup task and does not become Dynamic R across the four frozen trajectories.
Compressed historical/current context never develops into a durable unsupported shared operational state that drives downstream C/P effects.

divergence_patterns: G2 repeatedly inspects current, legacy and version surfaces under continuous compression but never delegates or mutates the repository.
G3 is a process-nondevelopment boundary; G4 remains an authorized cleanup boundary; G5 reaches the horizon without material mutation.
boundary_interpretation: Repeated review of old state under compression is not R when the user explicitly authorizes that review and no historical state gains new current authority.
A compressed context window does not become a system common pool merely because it repeatedly carries the same historical information; downstream adoption and operational reuse must be shown.
cross_group_semantic_synthesis.cohort_conclusion: LongLLMLingua X7-T3 is a four-group negative historical-control cohort. Compression repeatedly carries historical cleanup context, yet no old state is reauthorized into current semantic or execution permission. Together with X7-T1, this supports a clear boundary: structural compression can preserve or reshape context representation without itself creating shared operational inertia.

constraints: Cell-level Layer-C verdicts are sealed and are not modified by cohort synthesis.
